executive_assessment.text: Bafing evidence adds named departments, resource competition and gendered land/water-access constraints, with a source-stated seasonal mechanism rather than isolated climate causality.
Bouaké's 2018 water outage is a distinct historical vulnerability case. Pastoral infrastructure, local mediation and northern adaptation support are proposed capacities, not verified peace outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-04-01 reports: Lower rainfall reduced Bouaké's Loka reservoir (70% of city supply) in 2018; three weeks without piped water prompted emergency tankers and temporary migration. Northern shortages also constrained agriculture.
The Bafing proposal describes dry-season pasture/water scarcity concentrating herds and farms near residual resources, with crop damage and farmer-herder tensions across Koro, Touba and Ouaninou.
Bafing proposal consultations describe women accessing land mainly through husbands and dry-season distance barriers to water, with herders dependent on surface sources.

Source dated 2025 reports: Approved proposal plans water/fodder pastoral areas and community parks to reduce herd wandering and crop damage; it also supports local conflict-management mechanisms, climate-data use, and women/youth livelihood diversification.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 14 of 14 evidence records and 2 of 2 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The inspected climate–fragility material identifies potential risks but does not estimate causal effects or compare realized outcomes across regions.
The NDC’s adaptation measures are plans; delivery and effectiveness were not independently verified.
